providerTools.description: Small edits to the panels that exist: steps run in order as one change, and nothing applies unless every step works. For any arrangement of several panels (grids, columns, "4 panes", a new layout) use workspace_compose instead; at most one add per call. Step actions: focus (bring an area forward), resize (change: larger, smaller, maximize, restore, equal, or a share like 0.6), move (to: left, right, top, bottom, "beside <area>", or another area), keep (lock it where it is), label (name: what the person calls it), add (a new empty panel: to = side, area = the area it goes beside or "" for the window edge, name = optional), remove (take a panel away; its tabs move to the area in to, else the main editor; nothing closes). save_as: after the steps, save the result as a new named layout ("" to not save). Locked areas refuse changes; never try to unlock one.
providerTools.name: workspace_arrange

save_as.description: A new layout name to save the result as, else "".

area.description: An area from workspace_view (its name or id), or a plain description: "the code", "the chat", "the documentation", "the right panel", "this".

to.description: move, add and remove only, else "".

providerTools.description: Set the workspace to the state the person asked for, in one call. You only choose; Archivist finds the files, builds and sizes the panels, reuses what is open and applies it as one change the person can undo or redo. Never build layouts from moves or splits. mode patch (the usual case): the current panels stay where they are; a slot named like an existing panel gets its items there, a new name adds one panel at its position (left, right, top or bottom), and panels you don't name are left alone. Use it for "put the PDF beside the chat" or "add my notes on the right": arrangement auto, rows and columns 0. mode replace: a whole new arrangement from a recipe, only when the person asks for one ("4 panes", "three columns", "chat dominant", a template). Recipes: grid (rows x columns; "4 panes, chat bottom-left" is grid, rows 2, columns 2, chat at bottom-left; empty places become panels showing what was open), columns (left, center, right), rows (top, middle, bottom), split (one large panel at position primary, the rest stacked on one side: "chat dominant, three images stacked on the right"), stack (everything as tabs in one panel). Weights are relative (1 normal, 2 about twice); panels that don't fit become tabs. Files can be named by file name, path or an open tab's title; nothing closes. Templates fill their panels by name: focus_references (One large panel for the work, reference material at the side: Focus, References); chat_code (The code beside a conversation: Code, Chat); code_diff (A file next to the changes under review: Code, Changes); research_desk (Sources on the left, notes and references stacked on the right: Sources, Notes, Reference); agent_overview (Agent conversations across the top, their terminal and changes below: Agents, Terminal, Changes). save_as also saves it as a named layout ("" keeps it temporary). focus: a panel name to bring forward, only when asked.
providerTools.name: workspace_compose

holds.description: What kind of content belongs there; can be empty when items say it.

kind.description: file: a Library file. chat: a conversation ("" for this one). terminal: "" for the terminal, "new" for another. diff: changes under review. open_view: something already open, by view id or title.

library.description: "" for this chat's Library, else a Library or worktree name or id. Files keep the Library they belong to.

reference.description: file: Library-relative path or file id. chat: chat id or "". terminal: "" or "new". open_view: view id or title.

position.description: Where it goes. grid: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, top, bottom-center, r2c1. columns: left, center, right. rows: top, middle, bottom. split: primary for the large one; the first other panel's right/left/top/bottom says the side. : the next free place.

weight.description: Relative room: 1 normal, 2 about twice; 0 keeps the default.

providerTools.description: Named layouts: whole arrangements of panels the person can switch between. list shows the built-in and saved ones. apply switches to one by name (open tabs move into it; nothing closes; undoable); "try another" means apply a different one than the current layout. save stores the current arrangement under name (workspace_arrange save_as does this in the same call as the arranging). Saving over an existing name needs replace true, and only when the person said to replace it. rename (new_name) and delete work on the person's saved layouts only, and only when they ask.
providerTools.name: workspace_layout

replace.description: save only: replace a saved layout with the same name.

providerTools.description: Remember how the person likes their workspace, only when they state a preference (not for a one-off request). chat_location: bottom | docked ("I like my chat at the bottom"). main_editor: large | normal ("keep my main editor large"). rearranging: only_when_asked | when_helpful ("don't rearrange my windows unless I ask"). area_purpose: value is what a panel is for, e.g. documentation, and area names the panel ("use the right panel for documentation"). duration: always only when they say always, from now on, by default or describe a standing habit; otherwise this_session. clear forgets one; list shows them.
providerTools.name: workspace_preference

area.description: area_purpose only: the panel, e.g. "the right panel" or "this panel"; else "".

value.description: set: the value; clear: "" (or the purpose for area_purpose).

providerTools.description: Put the workspace back. before_task: how it was before you started rearranging ("put everything back", "restore my workspace", "put it back"). last_change: undo the most recent workspace change ("undo that", "switch back" after a change). redo: redo the change just undone ("redo", "actually, put it back how you had it"). saved_layout: apply one of the person's saved layouts by name. Open files, chats and terminals stay open; unsaved work is never closed.
providerTools.name: workspace_restore

layout.description: saved_layout only: the layout's name, else "".

providerTools.description: Open or bring forward files, chats or terminals in the workspace. Things already open are reused, not duplicated; several files share one area as tabs. Put every item in one call and leave where empty unless the person said where. Only call this when the person asked to see, open or bring something up; to find which files matter, use Library evidence first and show two to five.
providerTools.name: workspace_show

focus.description: Move keyboard focus there. Only when the person asked to switch to it.
